newsitem.title: USA: Public-private partnership key to sports projects.
newsitem.headline: Public-private partnership key to sports projects.

text.p: Local government officials stressed on Monday the importance of public-private partnerships in the funding of stadium and arena projects.
At a conference in San Francisco by the Bond Buyer newspaper, Denver and San Francisco officials said the private sector should play a major role in these projects.
"We in Denver believe that these sports facility investments only make sense if they're public-private partnerships," said Daniel Muse, Denver's city attorney.

"The city of Denver ... will not, in my judgement, support a sports facility project that requires the municipality or the metropolitan district to pay a disproportionate percentage of the costs," said Muse. "You will not see a 100 percent tax-supported or public-supported sports facility in Denver."
San Francisco Mayor Willie Brown said the driving force behind these projects should be the private sector since it is difficult to persuade voters to provide funding.
Both Brown and King County, Washington, Councilman Pete von Reichbauer said professional sports teams generate substantial tax revenues that benefit local and state governments.
"Professional sports generate a significant amount of money for a region," Reichbauer said.
